items.description:
BAJAUR: The district administration on Sunday imposed a ban on all kinds of public gatherings, hate speech against the state and the display of arms and weapons in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur for 30 days, invoking Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) owing to the prevailing law and order situation.
Section 144 is a provision in the CrPC that empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.

items.title: Ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says everyone knew about 'Sandpapergate'
items.description:
Former Australian Test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja over his “Sandpapergate” claims on Sunday, contradicting Pat Cummins’ denials that he knew nothing about the ball-tampering plot.
Sayers was on the tour of South Africa but did not play in the third Test at Cape Town, where sandpaper was used to help make the ball swing.
A Cricket Australia probe concluded only then-skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were in the know, with all sent home and banned.

items.description:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top spot in the latest edition of the world’s 500 most influential Muslims, alongside the Saudi king and crown prince and the Turkish president.

items.description:
